extracted.intended_audience: patentees, patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, patent office officials, and legal practitioners dealing with patents in the relevant jurisdiction
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and summarizes statutory standards and procedural requirements from a national Patents Act covering compulsory licences, assignment, revocation, infringement, evidence, state acquisition, appeals, and offences. Useful for practitioners wanting the legal criteria and procedural rules under the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for ordering a licence (compulsory licence grounds)
rubrics_metrics.description: The commissioner may order the grant of a licence where he is satisfied that: the demand for the patented article in the Republic is not being met to an adequate extent and on reasonable terms; the refusal of the patentee to grant a licence on reasonable terms prejudices trade/industry/agriculture or establishment of new trade/industry and it is in the public interest that a licence should be granted; or the demand in the Republic is being met by importation and the price charged by the patentee/licensee/agent is excessive relative to prices in countries where the article is manufactured under licence from the patentee or predecessor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The commissioner considers applications on their merits; the statutory grounds are the substantive predicates for compulsory licences. The text lists three distinct factual circumstances that may justify compulsory licensing: insufficient working locally, refusal to license prejudicing public interest, and excessive pricing combined with import dependence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to oppose a compulsory-licence application
rubrics_metrics.description: The patentee or any other person appearing from the register to be interested in the patent may, in the prescribed manner, oppose the application for a licence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opposition must follow prescribed procedure (form/timing). The statute explicitly affords interested parties standing to oppose compulsory-licence applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner’s discretion and possible conditions on granted licences
rubrics_metrics.description: When ordering a grant of a licence the commissioner shall consider the application on its merits and may order the grant on such conditions as he deems fit, including a condition precluding the licensee from importing into the Republic any patented articles. If not justified, he may refuse. A licence shall include a provision that, subject to adequate protection of the legitimate interests of the licensee, the licence shall, on patentee application, be terminated if the circumstances leading to its grant cease and are unlikely to recur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted conditions are broad; the commissioner may tailor terms to local policy (e.g., no-import clause). The commissioner may also deem a licence to have been granted from the application filing date (sub-s.7A). Orders should be aimed at avoiding the abuse found by the commissioner. Commissioner may amend or revoke licences and must regard relevant facts (risks to licensee, patentee R&D, usual licence terms) when fixing conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licences to be non-exclusive and non-transferable (with limited exception)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any licence granted under this section shall be non-exclusive and shall not be transferable except to a person to whom the business or part of the business in connection with which the rights under the licence were exercised has been transferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default statutory rule is non-exclusivity and non-transferability of compulsory licences; transfer is allowed only as part of a business transfer tied to the licence's exercise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors to consider when determining licence conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining the conditions on which any licence is granted the commissioner shall have regard to any relevant facts, including the risks to be undertaken by the licensee, the research and development undertaken by the patentee and the terms and conditions usually stipulated in licence agreements in respect of the subject-matter of the invention between persons who voluntarily enter into such agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit non-exhaustive list of substantive considerations. The commissioner must balance incentivizing patentee R&D and fair commercial risk/reward for licensee and consider market practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of contracts relating to licences on patent expiry/revocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Any contract so far as it relates to a licence under a patent shall terminate on the date on which the patent under which the licence was granted expires, is revoked or otherwise ceases to protect such invention; for contracts relating to licences under more than one patent, the part relating to each licence terminates when its patent ceases; the contract as a whole terminates when all such patents cease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statutory termination rule applies 'in default of an agreement to the contrary'. It does not affect separate contractual termination rights or conditions independently agreed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of licence in default of agreement (rights conferred)
rubrics_metrics.description: In default of an agreement to the contrary: (a) a licence to make a patented article shall carry with it the right to use or offer to dispose of or dispose of the patented article; (b) a licence to use or exercise a patented process shall carry with it the right to make, use or offer to dispose of or dispose of the product of the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute supplies implied ancillary rights that accompany manufacturing or process licences unless parties contract otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment and devolution of patent rights by operation of law
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to section 39(7), rights vested in a patentee or applicant shall be capable of assignment and of devolution by operation of law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General principle enabling transfer and succession of patent rights. Further statutory rules (recording, validity) apply to assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nullity of certain employment contract conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any condition in a contract of employment which requires an employee to assign to his employer an invention made by him otherwise than within the course and scope of his employment; or restricts the right of an employee in an invention made by him more than one year after termination of the contract of employment, shall be null and void.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects employee inventors from overbroad assignment clauses and prolonged post‑employment restrictions; statutory limits on employer contractual claims to employee inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form, registration and validity of assignments, attachments and hypothecations
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant or patentee may in writing assign rights; upon application in the prescribed manner and payment of prescribed fee the assignment shall be recorded in the register; unless recorded it shall not be valid except between the parties. A patent/application may be attached by recording the warrant/order in the register; attachment lapses after three years unless renewed. Hypothecation may be entered in the register on application. After entry of an attachment or hypothecation, the patentee/applicant shall not alienate or encumber the attached/hypothecated patent/application or grant licences under it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration is required for third-party validity and publicity; entries create public burdens and restrict alienation/licensing. There is prescribed procedural form/fee for recording; entries have temporal limits (attachments lapse in 3 years unless renewed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for revocation of a patent (exhaustive list in section)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may apply for revocation on specified grounds only: (a) patentee not entitled under section 27 to apply; (b) grant was in fraud of applicant's rights; (c) invention not patentable under section 25; (d) invention as illustrated/exemplified in the complete specification cannot be performed or does not lead to results/advantages set out; (e) complete specification does not sufficiently illustrate/describe/ascertain/exemplify the invention and manner of performance to enable a person skilled in the art to carry it out; (f) the claims of the complete specification are not clear or not fairly based on matter disclosed; (g) prescribed declaration contains a false material statement which patentee knew to be false at time of making; (h) application should have been refused under section 36; (i) complete specification claims a microbiological process/product and provisions of section 32(6) have not been complied with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statute enumerates substantive validity/formal grounds for revocation, including entitlement, fraud, patentability, sufficiency of disclosure, clarity and support of claims, and false declarations. Procedure requires service and lodging in prescribed manner; commissioner decides whether to revoke or uphold and may allow amendments consistent with section 51(6)/(7); commissioner may take into account patentee conduct re specification framing for costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner’s powers when patent revocation is sought
rubrics_metrics.description: On an application for revocation the commissioner shall decide whether the patent shall be revoked or whether and, if so, subject to what amendments of the specification or claims the patent shall be upheld; the commissioner shall not allow any amendment in conflict with section 51(6) or (7) and may take patentee conduct into consideration in awarding costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner has remedial power to conditionally uphold patents by permitting amendments; must respect statutory limits on allowable amendments and may penalize irresponsible drafting in costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent must be for one invention only (but no procedural objection allowed)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent shall be granted for one invention only, but no person may in any proceedings object to a patent on the ground that it comprises more than one invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule that patents are for a single invention is stated, but the statute bars objections in proceedings on the multiplicity ground—preserving other procedural routes for correcting divisionality at grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relief after revocation for fraud — inventor may obtain patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patent is revoked on the ground of fraud (or surrendered and revoked for fraud) the commissioner may, on application of the inventor (or assignee/legal representative), direct the grant to him of a patent for the whole or any part of the invention, bearing the same date as the patent so revoked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remedial measure to restore rights to true inventor following fraud-based revocation; commissioner has discretion to re‑issue patent to inventor/assignee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary surrender procedure and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: A patentee may offer to surrender his patent by notice in prescribed manner; registrar shall notify persons shown in the register to have an interest. Interested persons may lodge objection within prescribed time. If no objection or objection overruled after hearing, patent deemed revoked from date of receipt by registrar of offer; registrar shall advertise revocation and update register. Surrender offers not considered while infringement/revocation proceedings are pending except by consent of parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surrender is a formal statutory process with notice and opportunity to object; surrender triggers revocation and public notice; pending litigation blocks surrender absent consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceedings for infringement — who may sue, remedies, and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings for infringement may be instituted by the patentee (subject to section 53(3)) and shall be instituted and prosecuted in the prescribed manner. Remedies available to the plaintiff include an interdict, delivery up of infringing products (or articles of which the infringing product forms an inseparable part), and damages. Defendant may counterclaim for revocation and rely on any ground of revocation. Plaintiff must, before instituting proceedings, give notice to every licensee whose name is recorded in the register; such a licensee may intervene as co-plaintiff. In lieu of damages plaintiff may elect an amount calculated on the basis of a reasonable royalty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute prescribes standing, mandatory notice to recorded licensees, available equitable and monetary remedies, and allowance for counterclaims based on validity issues. Plaintiff has option to claim reasonable royalty instead of damages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on recovery of damages — lack of notice and marking rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A patentee is not entitled to recover damages from a defendant who proves that at the date of the infringement he was not aware and had no reasonable means of making himself aware of the existence of the patent. Marking an article with 'patent'/'patented' or similar words does not constitute notice unless accompanied by the patent number. Representation that an invention is patented without disclosing the patent number, and from whom the number is requested in writing by registered post, may prevent recovery of damages or interdict for a period until two months after the number is notified in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides defenses for innocent infringers and limits constructive notice via marking unless the patent number is shown. There is an express procedure limiting patentee relief where number was not supplied timely after written request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensation and remedies when reliance was placed on representations or requests
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who, after making a request for the patent number, expends money/time/labour with a view to making/using/importing the invention may apply to the commissioner for compensation for reasonable expenditure, and the commissioner may issue an order as he deems fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute recognizes reliance-induced loss and gives the commissioner remedial discretion to order compensation where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on damages owing to renewal fee default or post‑grant amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: If infringement occurred after failure to pay any prescribed renewal fee and before any extension, the commissioner may refuse to award damages. Where a specification amendment is allowed under section 51 the commissioner may refuse to award damages for acts before amendment and consider patentee conduct in framing the specification when exercising discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patentee procedural defaults or post‑grant corrective amendments can limit monetary recovery; commissioner has discretion and may consider equitable factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumptions for new substances/processes/products
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim for a process or apparatus for producing a product shall be construed as extending to such product when produced by the process/apparatus claimed. If the invention is a process for obtaining a new product, the same product produced by another person shall be deemed, unless contrary proved, to have been obtained by that process. The commissioner shall not require disclosure of any secret process used by such person if it would be unreasonable to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates evidentiary presumptions shifting burden to alleged infringer to prove an alternative process; protects trade secrets from unreasonable compelled disclosure in defending against the presumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relief when specification is partially valid (amendments and relief)
rubrics_metrics.description: If in infringement proceedings the commissioner finds some claims valid and others invalid, he may postpone any order on the counterclaim to enable patentee to amend the specification pursuant to conditions the commissioner imposes. After amendment, the commissioner may grant relief in respect of any claim previously found valid and infringed, subject to orders as to costs and date from which damages shall be calculated; the commissioner may consider patentee conduct in inserting or permitting invalid claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute provides a remedial pathway to correct defective claims and still permit recovery for valid claims, while allowing commissioner to impose equitable conditions and costs based on conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration of non-infringement (pre-emptive relief)
rubrics_metrics.description: A declaration that a person's use/making/offer/disposal/importation does not or would not constitute infringement may be made by the commissioner in proceedings between that person and the patentee (even if patentee has made no assertion) if it is proved that the person applied in writing to the patentee for a written acknowledgement to that effect and furnished full particulars of the process or article, and the patentee failed to give such an acknowledgement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanism for seeking declaratory relief; requires prior written request to patentee with full particulars. Costs of such proceedings awarded as commissioner deems fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts of non-infringement for non-commercial regulatory/experimental use (safe-harbour)
rubrics_metrics.description: It shall not be an act of infringement to make, use, exercise, offer to dispose of, dispose of or import the patented invention on a non-commercial scale solely for purposes reasonably related to obtaining, developing and submitting information required under any law that regulates manufacture/production/distribution/use/sale of any product. Possession of such material is limited to those regulatory purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit experimental/regulatory safe-harbour for activities necessary for regulatory approval (Bolar-type exception); use restricted to non-commercial, regulatory-related purposes only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies for groundless threats of infringement proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: A person threatened (by circular, advertisement or otherwise) with proceedings for infringement may institute proceedings to obtain a declaration that threats are unjustifiable, an interdict against continuance of threats, and recover damages sustained, unless the threatening person proves the acts threatened constitute, or would constitute if done, an infringement of a valid claim. Mere notification of existence of a patent for protecting interests is not, by itself, a threat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects persons from abusive/predatory assertion letters and threats; allows counter‑relief and counterclaims in the same proceedings for relief the defendant would have in separate infringement actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special rules for vessels, aircraft and land vehicles of convention countries
rubrics_metrics.description: The rights of a patentee shall not be deemed infringed by use on board a convention vessel of the patented invention in the body or machinery/accessories if the vessel comes into territorial waters temporarily/accidentally and the invention is used exclusively for the actual needs of the vessel; similar rule applies to convention aircraft/land vehicles temporarily/accidentally entering the Republic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory exception for temporary/accidental presence of foreign-registered vessels/aircraft/vehicles to avoid applying domestic patent exclusivity to transient uses strictly incidental to travel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register entries and proof of title — register as prima facie evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The person appearing from the register to be the proprietor or applicant shall, subject to any right shown to be vested in another, have power to deal with the patent/application as owner. The register shall be prima facie evidence of any matter directed to be entered therein. Documents or instruments not entered in the register (except for purposes of section 52) shall not be admitted in evidence in proof of title or interest unless the commissioner or a court, on good cause shown, otherwise directs. No person who does not appear from the register as having an interest shall be allowed to prove such interest in proceedings unless commissioner/court directs on good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register is the primary public record; entries confer presumptive ownership and control evidentiary protection; exceptions require good cause directions by commissioner/court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrar’s certificates and certified copies as prima facie evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: A certificate purporting to be signed by the registrar that an entry has or has not been made shall be prima facie evidence of the matters specified. A copy/extract purporting to be certified by the registrar and sealed with the patent office seal shall be admitted in evidence before the commissioner and in all courts without further proof or production of originals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitates evidentiary use of official records via certified copies and certificates; reduces need to produce originals in litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of validity and cost consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: If in proceedings a claim in a complete specification is found valid the commissioner or court may certify to that effect. If in subsequent proceedings the validity of that claim is unsuccessfully attacked, that party shall, unless otherwise directed, pay to the other party his full costs, charges and expenses as between patent agent/attorney and client so far as that claim is concerned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification creates a procedural/evidentiary benefit and potential cost penalty for unsuccessful re‑attacks on a claim previously certified as valid, shifting commercial risk to re‑litigant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals from registrar to commissioner and from commissioner to court — scope and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal lies from any decision of the registrar to the commissioner, who shall hear parties and issue such order as he deems fit. Any party to proceedings before the commissioner may appeal to the court against any order/decision. Appeals shall be noted/prosecuted in the manner prescribed for appeals against a civil order of a single judge; the court may confirm/vary/set aside, remit the matter for further evidence/information, take measures for a just/speedy/inexpensive settlement and make such orders as to costs as justice may require.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies hierarchical appellate routes and procedural cross‑references to civil appeal rules and Supreme Court Act sections; courts have broad remedial powers including remittal for supplementing evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreement to accept commissioner’s decision as final and binding
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties in any proceedings before the commissioner may agree in writing prior to hearing to submit the matter for final decision to the commissioner; where there is such an agreement the order or decision of the commissioner shall be binding, final and conclusive and shall not be subject to appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may contractually waive appellate rights by prior written agreement to accept commissioner’s final determination; procedural formalities required (written agreement, prescribed manner to apply).

rubrics_metrics.name: State acquisition, secrecy and compensation for inventions/patents
rubrics_metrics.description: The Minister may acquire any invention or patent on such terms as agreed. Proprietor of armaments-related inventions must assign to Minister of Defence if called upon. The Minister of Defence (or relevant Minister of State) may direct that an invention and manner of performance be kept secret; applications/specifications/drawings relating to such invention shall be sealed and contents not divulged without written permission. A patent made out may be delivered to the Minister and be State property; the Minister shall pay reasonable compensation as agreed or in default determined by arbitration or, if parties agree, by the commissioner. When secrecy orders are withdrawn interrupted procedural steps may continue and periods elapsed while order was in force shall not be taken into account in computing prescribed times. If proprietor suffers loss/damage due to secrecy, Minister pays reasonable compensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad state powers to acquire and require secrecy for national interest/defence, with mandatory sealing and compensation mechanisms; procedural protections for applicants whose prosecution was suspended by secrecy orders (time not counted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of Minister to require inventions to be kept secret in national interest
rubrics_metrics.description: If Minister is of opinion that in the national interest an application/specification/drawing or other document relating to an invention should be kept secret, he may order the registrar to keep the invention secret and notify the applicant; provisions similar to defence assignments apply and compensation may be payable for loss or damage suffered by proprietor due to secrecy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the national-security/other public-interest secrecy mechanism and associated compensation; withdrawal of orders allows resumption of interrupted prosecution without penalizing statutory time limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offences and penalties for false entries, false copies and tendering false evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who makes or causes to be made a false entry in the register; makes or causes to be made a writing falsely purporting to be a copy of an entry; or produces/tenders as evidence any such false entry or copy knowing it to be false, is guilty of an offence and on conviction liable to a fine not exceeding R1 000 or imprisonment up to 12 months or both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criminalizes falsification of official patent registries/documents; penalties set out (monetary and custodial) to deter fraud in public records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalty for making false statements to deceive or influence registrar/commissioner/officer
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who, for the purpose of deceiving the registrar/commissioner/officer or procuring/influencing anything under the Act, makes a false statement or representation knowing it to be false, shall be guilty of an offence and liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding R1 000 or imprisonment up to 12 months or both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criminal sanction for willful misrepresentation aimed at patent office processes or decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on trafficking in patents by patent office officers/employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Any officer or employee of the patent office who buys, sells, acquires or traffics in any invention or patent or any right under a patent shall be guilty of an offence and liable to a fine not exceeding R500. Every purchase, sale, acquisition or assignment by or to such officer/employee shall be null and void. Exceptions do not apply to the inventor or to acquisitions by bequest or devolution by operation of law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintains integrity and avoids conflict of interest of patent office staff; transactions by staff in patents/inventions are criminalized and void.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalty for improper use of words 'patent office'
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who uses on his place of business or on any document the words 'patent office' or other words suggesting official connection with the patent office shall be guilty of an offence and liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding R100 or to imprisonment not exceeding three months or both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents misleading representations of official endorsement or affiliation with the patent office; relatively modest penalties provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties for false representations that an article is patented or subject to a patent application
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who falsely represents that any article is a patented article, or represents that any article is the subject of a patent application knowing no such application has been made or that an application made has been refused/withdrawn/lapsed, shall be guilty of an offence and liable to a fine not exceeding R1 000 or imprisonment up to 12 months or both. Disposing of an article marked 'patent' or similar is deemed to be such a representation unless done in good faith in ordinary course and identity of source is disclosed when called upon. An aggrieved person may apply to the commissioner for continuation of an interdict against such representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory prohibition against misleading commercial assertions of patent protection; includes deemed representation by markings and provides limited good-faith defenses and remedial avenues for aggrieved parties.
